what: Steam fogs up glass pieces (clip-path polygon shapes). A frost layer that blurs what’s behind by 14px (ink 14%) is covered by a mask in the piece’s shape, and rubbing with the cursor wipes it away with a round brush of radius 56px (stamped every 12px). Beside wiped spots, droplets form with 12% probability and run down (acceleration .01+.002r, sideways wobble .35px), wiping the line they pass again, and pooled drops (up to 7) slide once they grow. From 2.4s after the last wipe, the frost returns (dt/2.8 per frame). When more than 35% has been wiped from the start, fx:wiped fires once. On fx:play, it appears straight over .72s after 1.5s.

options.delay: Delay after fx:play before appearing (sec), default 1.5
options.refog: Pause before frost starts forming again (s), default 2.4
options.threshold: fx:wiped fires at this wiped ratio, default .35
options.auto: If on, fx:play right after attaching
options.fx:play / fx:reset: Events sent to the element — appear and spin / hide and stop. When the wiped ratio passes the threshold, the element emits fx:wiped

from.where: index.html people section — original data-fog-glass·data-fog-layers (four broken display-case glass pieces that fog over 1.5s after the section turns on, over CURTAIN_DURATION .72s · brush 56px · refog 2.4s · threshold .35 · frost #2B2B2B 14% + blur 14px · absent on Safari, phones and reduced motion)

note: The frost and droplet panels go in as siblings right after the piece (with the piece’s clip-path, the blur behind its bottom face looks empty) — the piece’s parent must be the position reference. The mask is re-baked as a PNG on every wipe and every .1s while droplets run. It is not attached on touch devices or with reduced motion (the original is desktop-only too)
